subject: Performance acceptance playbook — TTFT & streaming bench plan and results
summary: Mutual action plan and acceptance criteria for streaming chat TTFT + latency benchmarking. Includes plan, runner configs, preliminary results and sign-off timeline for pilot and dedicated onboarding.
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Performance acceptance playbook — initial MAP and bench plan

Ethan — attaching the performance acceptance playbook (redwood_bench_plan_v1.xlsx) as discussed on the call. High level plan below and a couple of asks so we can slot runs into your pilot window next week.

Scope (short):
- Workload: chat/text generation (streaming) for BrightHealth triage assistant
- Metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token) + streaming token latency; aggregated p50/p95/p99 and throughput (tokens/sec) at targeted concurrency
- Targets (preliminary acceptance): p50 TTFT <= 110ms, p95 TTFT <= 320ms, p99 TTFT <= 900ms; streaming token p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 950ms at pilot concurrency
- Concurrency profiles: 1/5/10/25/50 concurrent sessions (session = active streaming chat; avg prompt length ~ 160 tokens; typical total sequence 600 tokens)

Planned artifacts we will produce for each run: time-series traces, aggregated percentiles (TTFT + per-token), CPU/GPU utilization, flamegraph of host-side stalls, and the raw CSV (bench_results_YYYYMMDD.csv).

Operational asks from BrightHealth:
1) Agree slot for a 2-hour dedicated run (we propose 2028-06-10 09:00–11:00 PT)
2) Provide 3 representative prompt sets (clinical triage + insurance FAQ + appointment scheduling) or permission to use our anonymized templates
3) Confirm network region (preferred us-west1) and whether we should test via your VPC peering / private endpoint or public demo endpoint

We’ll run the baseline on hosted Redwood (standard model, 16k context) and a second pass on the dedicated instance you are evaluating. Jonas will drop the load config and runner details in a follow-up.

Next steps: please review the attached playbook and confirm the window and sample prompts. If you want a narrower acceptance bar for p99, call it out and we’ll prioritize additional tuning (batching / KV caching / quant quant).

— Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachment: redwood_bench_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet: test matrix, SLOs, data templates)

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brighthealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Taylor <mark.taylor@brighthealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-02T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance playbook — initial MAP and bench plan

Thanks Monica — the plan looks reasonable. We can do the run on 2028-06-10 09:00–11:00 PT. A couple of clarifications:

- We will provide 3 prompt sets by EOD 2028-06-06 (clinical-triage.csv, claims-faq.csv, scheduling.csv)
- We will test over VPC peering (private endpoint); our infra team will create a test subnet and share the IP allowlist
- Security ask: do you need a completed pen-test report or SOC artifact before we run on our VPC? Mark (CISO) is on copy — can you confirm minimal docs required?

Also, what is the recommended binning for token-level percentiles? We prefer 10ms buckets for streaming latency if that helps.

— Ethan
Ethan Cole
Staff Product Manager, BrightHealth
ethan.cole@brighthealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-03T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance playbook — load harness and runner config

Ethan — quick technical follow-up. Attached is the load test config (load_test_config.yaml) and a small streaming notebook (stream_bench.ipynb) that runs the same harness we’ll use in the production runs. Key points:

- Runner provides per-session RTT and per-token delta timestamps. We compute TTFT as timestamp of first token event minus request-send time.
- Defaults: 10ms token bucket resolution; sample rate 100% for TTFT and 10% for full token traces (we attach sampled full traces separately).
- We’ll spin up a dedicated client pool with ephemeral identities to mimic your real session concurrency profile.
- Endpoints: we’ll provide a test API key scoped to the bench account and a private endpoint hostname via your peering.

If you prefer different sampling or token bucket widths, tell us and we’ll update the config. For the main run, we’ll record GPU-side profiling (NVIDIA Nsight counters) and host flamegraphs.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachment: load_test_config.yaml, stream_bench.ipynb

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance playbook — preliminary run and quick findings

Ethan — we ran the pilot window yesterday morning as agreed (09:00–11:00 PT). Attaching the CSV of raw results (bench_results_20280610.csv) and a quick flamegraph (flamegraph_20280610.svg). High-level summary below:

Baseline (hosted):
- Concurrency 1: p50 TTFT 72ms / p95 180ms / p99 420ms
- Concurrency 10: p50 TTFT 98ms / p95 300ms / p99 860ms
- Streaming token p95 260ms / p99 730ms (token-level measured at 10ms bins)

Dedicated candidate (same model, pinned variant):
- Concurrency 1: p50 TTFT 65ms / p95 160ms / p99 400ms
- Concurrency 25: p50 TTFT 135ms / p95 360ms / p99 1100ms (noticeable p99 spike)
- Streaming token p95 330ms / p99 1120ms at 25 conc.

Observations / immediate hypotheses:
- p99 growth driven by tail serialization on host-side copy / kernel fusion mismatch for long sequences. Flamegraph points to several short-lived stalls during KV-cache lookup under high concurrent KV cache churn.
- GPU utilization remains healthy (~78% avg) but host-side CPU shows spikes correlated with token emission bursts.

Action items from our side:
1) Re-run with increased batching window (Jonas will push new config) to see if p99 comes down without impacting p50/p95.
2) Test with KV-cache warmup (keep-alive sessions) to ensure cache hits under steady traffic.
3) Produce trimmed acceptance report for your review (we’ll publish annotated CSV and a short doc).

We flagged the p99 issue with the product team; if BrightHealth needs a stricter p99 requirement we can explore quant/ASAP kernel fallbacks and a short canary on dedicated hardware.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

Attachments: bench_results_20280610.csv, flamegraph_20280610.svg

From: Mark Taylor <mark.taylor@brighthealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brighthealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance playbook — preliminary run and quick findings

Hannah / Monica — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A couple of items from security/ops:
- Pen-test: we do not require a fresh pen-test before the bench run; a SOC2 Type II report from Redwood is sufficient for our risk board to approve the private endpoint test (I have the intake checklist ready). Please send SOC artifacts via the secure doc link.
- Regarding p99: our pilot acceptance requires p99 TTFT <= 1000ms at the 25-concurrency profile. The dedicated candidate breaches that in the preliminary run (1100ms). Can Redwood provide a canary plan and a fallback model (smaller context) if we see regression in production?

If you can provide a timeline by EOD 2028-06-14 for the re-run and potential mitigation steps, we can lock the pilot start for 2028-06-20.

— Mark
Mark Taylor
CISO, BrightHealth
mark.taylor@brighthealth.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brighthealth.com>, Mark Taylor <mark.taylor@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance playbook — timeline, MAP items, and sign-off

Thanks Mark — noted on SOC2. I’ll share the secure link for SOC artifacts separately this afternoon. Quick update and MAP-level mutual action items so we can close on the pilot timeline: 

Mutual Action Plan (executive view):
- BrightHealth: provide prompt sets (by 2028-06-06 — done), open test subnet + allowlist (done), confirm pilot start date (requested 2028-06-20)
- Redwood: deliver re-run with updated batching and KV warmup config (target complete 2028-06-14), produce annotated acceptance report (2028-06-15), provide canary/fallback plan and dedicated capacity onboarding checklist (2028-06-16)

Acceptance criteria (finalized):
- p95 TTFT <= 350ms across target concurrency profile
- p99 TTFT <= 1000ms at peak concurrency (25 sessions)
- Streaming token p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 1100ms
- No functional regressions on output quality (we will verify via the prompt test set)

Planned close timeline:
- 2028-06-14: Redwood runs re-test and posts results (Hannah’s team) — in progress
- 2028-06-15: Redwood delivers annotated acceptance report and sign-off pack
- 2028-06-16: Redwood sends dedicated onboarding checklist and cost estimate for reserved capacity
- 2028-06-20: Pilot begins (traffic shaping + canary policies in place). BrightHealth to approve final go/no-go by 2028-06-23.

Open asks from us:
1) Mark: confirm that SOC2 artifact link will satisfy procurement (we will send it now)
2) Ethan: confirm 2028-06-20 pilot start, and whether you want the initial 24 hours ramped traffic or a hard cutover

If we can get Mark + Ethan to confirm the two asks, we’ll mark the MAP as on-track and close the commercial milestone.

Best — Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: (SOC artifacts link to be sent via secure channel)
